Smiling guests clap and turn toward the newly open doorway, while someone may guide the group inside. Daylight or entrance lights catch the ribbon’s sheen. Camera shutters, applause, greetings, and the small snip occur in sequence.

At a prepared building site, workers in helmets, boots, gloves, and high-visibility clothing guide wet concrete from a pump hose into timber or metal formwork. One worker grips the heavy hose with both hands as the thick grey mix flows downward in uneven folds; others use shovels or rakes to spread it without stepping into unsupported areas. A vibrating probe briefly hums inside the mix, settling it around reinforcement and bringing small bubbles to the surface. Faces stay focused, with short spoken directions between movements. Harsh daylight shows damp patches and aggregate in the slurry. Pump rumble, engine noise, scraping tools, and bootsteps fill the site.

In a workshop, a welder wears a lowered welding helmet, gloves, long sleeves, and sturdy boots while joining two clamped pieces of metal. They steady the torch near the seam, start the arc, and move along it at a controlled pace. A bright blue-white point of light appears at the contact area; small orange sparks shoot outward, curve down under gravity, and fade on the floor. The welder stops, lifts the torch away, and waits before inspecting the bead through the helmet. Nearby workers face away or stay behind welding screens. The arc crackles sharply over a low ventilation hum, with intermittent metallic taps.

In a modest Iraqi apartment, the electrician stands beside an open wall switch box, with insulated screwdrivers and a voltage tester on a small stool. He switches off the circuit breaker, tests the wires, then loosens a terminal and trims a frayed end. Copper bends stiffly as he strips the insulation and secures the wire under the screw. His brow tightens while he works; the resident watches from a few steps away. Plastic clicks, a screwdriver turns with a faint scrape, and the cover plate snaps back on. Only then does he restore power and test the switch under warm ceiling light.

Under a kitchen sink, the plumber kneels on a folded cloth beside a shallow bucket. He closes the water valves, twists the curved drain trap loose and lowers it carefully; a little cloudy water drips into the bucket with hollow taps. He wipes the threads, clears a small blockage and tightens the trap by hand before giving it a short turn with pliers. His sleeves are pushed up and his face stays focused. The homeowner leans near the doorway, watching the first test flow. Water rushes into the basin, the pipe gives a soft gurgle, and both look underneath for leaks.

In an open-front garage, a car rests on jack stands above a concrete floor marked with old oil stains. The mechanic lies on a low wheeled creeper and rolls beneath it, holding a small work lamp in one hand. He steadies a wrench with both hands, pulls until a bolt releases, then lowers a metal cover into a parts tray. The wrench clicks; the cover lands with a light clang. His expression is intent, and he squints toward the lit underside. A colleague crouches outside the car, listening and passing him a socket. Daylight cuts across the garage entrance while a fan hums nearby.

Inside a tailoring shop, a customer stands straight in front of a mirror wearing a shirt and trousers. The tailor drapes a flexible measuring tape around the chest, holds it level without pulling tight and reads the number. He notes it in a small book, then measures the shoulders, waist and sleeve length in turn. The customer lowers his arms when asked and glances at his reflection; the tailor studies each line with a calm, concentrated face. Tape slides against fabric, a pencil scratches paper, and hangers click softly on a rail. Bright shop lights show the folds and seams clearly.

At the edge of a shaded Iraqi sidewalk, the shoe shiner sits behind a compact wooden box fitted with a raised footrest. A customer places one leather shoe on it. The shiner brushes away dust in quick strokes, spreads a thin layer of polish with a cloth and buffs the toe until it catches a bright reflection. The customer's other foot stays on the pavement, and both watch the finish take shape. Bristles rasp against leather; the polishing cloth makes a brisk, soft swish. Traffic passes behind them, while small tins, brushes and a folded rag remain neatly arranged beside the box.

At a street-side cart in Iraq, a vendor turns small pieces of seasoned meat on a flat metal griddle. One hand works a spatula while the other steadies an open bread roll. He presses the meat briefly, scoops it into the bread, adds sliced tomato and herbs, then wraps the sandwich in paper. Oil spits in tiny bursts and the spatula scrapes sharply across the hot surface. His face is alert as he checks the browning; a waiting customer watches the sandwich and reaches for it with a smile. Steam rises into the evening light, with traffic noise beyond the cart.

An ice cream vendor stands beside a small wheeled cart with a shaded lid and colourful pictures of frozen treats on its sides. He rings a handbell once, lifts the lid and reaches into the cold compartment for a wrapped ice cream. A child points to a picture while an adult stands close beside them; the vendor checks the choice and hands the treat over with an easy smile. The wrapper crinkles as the child takes it. The lid drops shut with a muted thump, the cart wheels rattle slightly when he shifts it, and late-afternoon sunlight glints on the metal handle.

Near a busy public walkway, a balloon seller holds a cluster of helium-filled balloons tied to a weighted handle. Round red, yellow and blue balloons bob above his head, tugging their thin strings taut whenever a breeze crosses the street. A child points upward; the seller separates one string from the bundle, loops it securely around the child's wrist and lets the balloon rise to the string's length. The child smiles and looks up while the accompanying adult watches the knot. The balloons rub together with faint squeaks, nearby footsteps and voices fill the background, and soft daylight shines through their coloured surfaces.

At a fairground stall, a vendor pours a small scoop of coloured sugar into the spinning metal head at the centre of a wide stainless-steel bowl. The motor hums; melted sugar shoots through tiny openings and cools into fine strands along the bowl’s rim. Keeping fingers clear of the hot head, the vendor turns a paper stick around the rim, then lifts and rotates it to gather a loose, cloud-shaped puff. The strands stretch lightly before settling onto the stick. A waiting child leans forward and smiles; an adult beside them watches the vendor’s hands. Warm stall lights show the candy’s pale pink translucence against the darker evening background.
